Text 1

In 1971, petroleum engineers analyzing auctions for offshore oil leases described a phenomenon now known as the winner’s curse. When numerous bidders compete for an item whose true value is uncertain, each must estimate that value, and the highest bid tends to come from whoever overestimated it most. Consequently, even when bidders’ estimates are accurate on average, the winner frequently pays more than the item ultimately proves to be worth.

Text 2

Each year, National Football League teams take turns selecting promising college players in a draft, and teams frequently surrender several later selections in order to move up and choose earlier. Researchers Cade Massey and Richard Thaler compared the cost of early picks, in traded selections and in players’ salaries, with the value the chosen players actually provide. Top picks, they found, are significantly overvalued, a pattern inconsistent with efficient markets.
items.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the findings presented in Text 2?
options: By arguing that the findings are surprising, since teams with long experience in drafting players should not consistently overpay
By suggesting that the teams willing to pay the most to move up in the draft may be those that most overestimate the players available
By pointing out that a draft differs from an auction because football teams cannot simply use money to bid against one another for the players they want
By claiming that football teams, unlike bidders for oil leases, tend to estimate the value of what they acquire accurately on average
items.explanation: Text 1 explains that when bidders compete for an item of uncertain value, “the highest bid tends to come from whoever overestimated it most,” so winners often overpay. Text 2 reports that teams “surrender several later selections” to move up and that top picks are “significantly overvalued.” The author of Text 1 would see this as the winner’s curse at work: the teams that pay the most for early picks may be the ones that most overestimate the players.

A.why_wrong: Text 1’s author explains overpaying as a built-in result of competitive bidding, even when estimates are “accurate on average,” so the findings would not seem surprising.

C.why_wrong: Neither text argues that the draft cannot be compared with an auction; Text 2 notes that teams pay for picks with other selections and with salaries.

D.why_wrong: This reuses Text 1’s phrase about estimates being accurate on average to set football teams against oil bidders, a contrast neither text draws.

sources.what: Massey and Thaler 2013, Management Science 59(7), The Loser’s Curse: NFL draft-day trades, player performance and compensation; top draft picks significantly overvalued, inconsistent with rational expectations and efficient markets

Text 1

Viewers trained in European art sometimes find Chinese landscape scrolls puzzling. Since the Renaissance, European painters have generally used linear perspective, which presents a scene as it would appear to someone standing at one fixed point. Judged by that standard, a painting in which the viewer seems to look up at a mountain’s peaks while also looking down into its valleys can appear inconsistent, as if the painter had not mastered depth.

Text 2

Guo Xi, a court painter of China’s Northern Song dynasty, created landscapes such as Early Spring (1072) that combine multiple viewpoints. This approach, sometimes called “floating perspective,” frees the eye to travel through the landscape. Guo Xi even named his method of combining views “the angle of totality.” It was an alternative way of representing space, not a failed attempt at the European one.
items.stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely regard the judgment of Chinese landscape painting described in Text 1?
options: As unfair, because European painters of the same period also combined several viewpoints in their landscapes
As outdated, because Chinese painters in later centuries began using linear perspective in their work
As reasonable, because Guo Xi’s paintings were meant to be viewed only by members of the court
As misguided, because the combined viewpoints in such paintings were a deliberate technique rather than a mistake
items.explanation: Text 1 describes viewers who judge Chinese landscapes by the standard of linear perspective and conclude that the painter “had not mastered depth.” The author of Text 2 explains that Guo Xi combined viewpoints on purpose, naming his method “the angle of totality,” and calls it “an alternative way of representing space, not a failed attempt at the European one.” The author would therefore regard the judgment as misguided.

A.why_wrong: Text 2 might call the judgment unfair, but it never says European painters combined viewpoints; its reason is that the Chinese method was deliberate.

B.why_wrong: Neither text says Chinese painters later adopted linear perspective.

C.why_wrong: Text 2 disagrees with the judgment, and neither text says who was allowed to view Guo Xi’s paintings.

sources.what: Guo Xi (c. 1020 to c. 1090), Northern Song court painter; Early Spring (1072) shows multiple perspectives he called the angle of totality, also called floating perspective, displacing the viewer’s static eye

Text 1

Bossa nova, the musical style that emerged in Rio de Janeiro during the late 1950s, owes its distinctive sound primarily to guitarist and singer João Gilberto. Gilberto adapted one rhythmic layer of a samba percussion ensemble for the guitar, plucking a simplified samba beat with his fingers. On his 1959 album Chega de Saudade, that guitar pattern became the foundation of an entirely new style.

Text 2

Gilberto’s guitar may be bossa nova’s signature, but the music’s character derived equally from the songs he performed. Composer Antônio Carlos Jobim, collaborating with lyricist Vinicius de Moraes on compositions such as “Chega de Saudade,” introduced sophisticated new harmonies to the samba song. Without Jobim’s compositions, Gilberto’s innovative rhythm would have had far less to carry.
items.stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?
options: Bossa nova became popular in the United States before it became popular in Brazil.
Bossa nova’s guitar rhythm mattered more to its sound than its harmonies did.
Bossa nova was built in part on musical elements drawn from samba.
Gilberto rarely performed the songs that Jobim composed with Vinicius de Moraes.
items.explanation: The authors disagree about what mattered most in bossa nova, but both link it to samba. Text 1 says Gilberto played “a simplified samba beat,” and Text 2 says Jobim “introduced sophisticated new harmonies to the samba song.” Both would therefore agree that bossa nova was built in part on musical elements drawn from samba.

A.why_wrong: Neither text discusses bossa nova’s popularity in the United States.

B.why_wrong: The author of Text 1 might agree, but the author of Text 2 argues that the music’s character “derived equally from the songs he performed.”

D.why_wrong: Text 2 says the music’s character “derived equally from the songs he performed,” naming Jobim and de Moraes’s “Chega de Saudade,” which is also the title of Gilberto’s album in Text 1.
